data.title: The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer :: The Coca-Cola Company (KO)
data.summary: The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer Elkins to Succeed John Murphy, Who Will Continue to Serve as President of the Company ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- The Coca-Cola Company today announced that David Elkins, a finance leader with extensive experience across global pharmaceuticals and consumer products companies, will become executive vice president and chief financial officer of Coca-Cola April 2, 2027, succeeding John Murphy. [...] Georgia, Fuze Tea, Gold Peak and Ayataka. Our juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverage brands include Minute Maid, Simply, innocent, Del Valle, fairlife and Santa Clara. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across [...] Murphy, 64, intends to retire in 2027, with timing determined later to allow for a smooth and orderly leadership transition for the CFO role. Murphy, who has been CFO since 2019, has been working with company leadership for some time to prepare for the succession process. Murphy will continue to serve as president, focusing on key enterprise priorities in 2027, in addition to the CFO transition. As CFO, Elkins’ oversight will include finance, global strategy and Enterprise Services.

data.title: Coca-Cola hires pharma vet for CFO
data.summary: Coca-Cola picked pharmaceutical industry veteran David Elkins to be its next CFO, awarding him one-time compensation of nearly $11 million, according to a Monday securities filing. He succeeds John Murphy, who will step down from the finance chief post on April 2 but remain as president. Murphy will retire later in 2027, Coca-Cola said in a press release announcing the appointment. [...] The beverage business announced the CFO transition approximately a month after it raised its full-year 2026 guidance during its most recent earnings call, with Coca-Cola now expecting earnings per share growth of 11% compared to its previous range of 9% to 10%, [...] The business also now anticipates free cash flow of $13 billion for the full year, compared to previous guidance of $12.4 billion, according to its third quarter earnings report published Oct. 27. Capital expenditures remained unchanged from prior guidance at about $2.2 billion.

data.title: Coca-Cola appoints Bristol Myers executive as finance chief | Fort Worth Star-Telegram
data.summary: Business Coca-Cola appoints Bristol Myers executive as finance chief Nov 23 (Reuters) - Coca-Cola said on Monday David Elkins will become chief financial officer in April next year, succeeding John Murphy, who is set to retire. Murphy, 64, has been the beverage maker's financial chief since 2019 and has worked with company leadership to prepare for the succession, the company said, adding that his retirement date will be determined later. [...] Elkins, 58, currently serves as chief financial officer of pharmaceutical company Bristol Myers Squibb. The beverage maker late last month raised its annual profit forecast as soft drink demand held up in markets including India and Brazil, even as it warned of accelerating cost pressures and persistent consumer weakness into 2027. (Reporting by Neil J Kanatt in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid) Copyright Reuters or USA Today via Reuters Connect [...] This story was originally published November 23, 2026 at 3:57 PM.

data.title: Coca-Cola ditched AI for its new holiday ad - Fast Company
data.summary: After two years of AI-generated holiday ads that spawned plenty of real-world backlash, Coca-Cola went live-action for its latest holiday campaign. Coca-Cola’s new spot “Enjoy Joy” shows real human actors as friends and family engaged in fall and winter activities, like playing football and having a turkey dinner. It ends with the word Enjoy written in its new tall, serifed typeface. [...] Coca-Cola was an early adopter to AI marketing, offering an online, AI-generated holiday card maker in 2023. It followed that up with its AI-generated remakes of “Holidays Are Coming” in 2024. Despite online criticism, it released yet another AI-generated ad last year that showed AI-generated snowscapes, winter creatures, and localized elements for geo-specific media buys, like a “Welcome to Boston” billboard in Boston. [...] Still, the company says viewers shouldn’t read into the choice too much. “This does not signal a broader shift, as Coca-Cola continues to explore different creative approaches and emerging technologies to bring its storytelling to life,” says Madison Chandler, a spokesperson for the company. “Human storytellers remain at the center of the creative process, with AI serving as a tool to support and enhance creative expression where appropriate.”
